basis: Congenital cutaneous constriction bands, nail deformities and associated hand malformations define the syndrome.
Degeneration affects the eye; extraocular neurologic disease is not shared across this umbrella.
Congenital heart disease and skeletal features characterize the group. Neurologic and skin involvement vary substantially by subtype.
Infection directly inflames and damages bone; adjacent marrow involvement does not establish a separate blood-cell disorder.
Cowden mucocutaneous and oral papillomas define the phenotype; thyroid nodules reported in 1/2. Predisposed carcinomas are separate diseases.
Meningeal tumor at the anterior foramen magnum.
An ocular motility disorder; an underlying neurologic cause is not established by this concept.
Inherited alpha-globin disorder affects red cells; severe systemic complications are not shared across the spectrum.
Limb-bone, cutaneous syndactyly and nail defects define the syndrome; hydronephrosis and vesicoureteral reflux reported in 1/3.
Autoinflammatory disease; rash and conjunctivitis are transient. Uveitis/arthritis reports are isolated; renal amyloidosis occurred in 1/26.
Usually arises in pleural mesothelium; peritoneal origin represents a minority subtype.
Direct peripheral nerve damage defines diabetic polyneuropathy; diabetes is the underlying separately diagnosed metabolic disease.
Congenital ichthyosis and palmoplantar keratoderma reflect a skin-barrier disorder; no systemic metabolic disease is established.
Cerebral arterial stenosis defines moyamoya; ischemic stroke occurred in 2/2. Glaucoma is separately diagnosed.
Microcephaly and developmental impairment define the syndrome; lipoatrophy, thin skin and sparse hair occur in 80–99%. Feeding difficulty alone adds no GI axis.
Severe combined immunodeficiency with profound T-cell deficiency in 11/11; organ infections are separately diagnosed complications.
Clonal mast-cell proliferation directly infiltrates the skin; systemic organ infiltration is not part of this cutaneous subtype.
Lipid-metabolism defect causes ichthyosis and CNS disease; reduced acuity 19/19 and retinal atrophy 5/9 support ocular damage. Contractures omitted under cap.
Congenital absence of whole limbs or terminal limb segments defines the disorder.
Granulosa-cell tumor arises from gonadal endocrine sex cord-stromal lineage. Gynecomastia (~25%) and metastases (~20%) add no axes.
Autoimmune destruction and atrophy of the thyroid cause hypothyroidism.
Acquired hemophilia due to factor XI inhibitors is an immune-mediated coagulation disorder.
Malignant astrocytic tumor originates in and infiltrates the central nervous system.
Sensorineural deafness and persistent skin/hair pigment abnormalities define the syndrome; intellectual disability reported in 1/1. Ocular findings are occasional.
Congenital herniation of meninges and brain through a defining cranial bone defect.
